description.html: This decoration is inspired by the famous Aztec calendar, a stone disc with the face of the sun at its center. The beige version looks like roughly carved sandstone: a face sits in the middle, surrounded by a ring of small glyphs, and rays in the shape of an eight-pointed star reach toward the edge, framed by a row of small circles. The relief is shallow and even, so the disc looks calm and natural next to sand, stones and dry branches.

It fits best in desert and semi-arid terrariums, for example for a bearded dragon, leopard gecko or desert snakes, where the beige tones match the substrate. If you prefer warmer, reddish tones and deeper relief, take a look at the terracotta version of the Aztec sun stone.

You can lean the disc against the back or side wall of the terrarium as a relief ornament, or lay it on the substrate as a flat surface for your animal to walk across. When leaning it, bury the bottom edge in the substrate or wedge it with a stone so it cannot slip and fall on the animal. The space behind a tilted disc can also serve as an extra shelter.
Before placing it, rinse the disc with lukewarm water and let it dry completely. Remove dust and substrate residue with a soft brush; the decoration is easy to take out and wash.
